# Resource: stripe_transfer

Money moved from the platform's balance to a connected account. Only `description` and `metadata` change after creation. Reverse a transfer with `stripe_transfer_reversal`.

~> A transfer can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete a transfer; reverse it with a `stripe_transfer_reversal`, which destroy does not create. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the transfer, fail at plan time. To stop managing a transfer, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Move test funds from the platform's available balance to a connected account.
resource "stripe_transfer" "payout_share" {
  amount         = 1500
  currency       = "usd"
  destination    = "acct_123"
  transfer_group = "order-1"
  description    = "Seller share of order 1"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) representing how much to transfer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO code for currency](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `destination` - (Required) The ID of a connected Stripe account. <a href="/docs/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers">See the Connect documentation</a> for details. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `source_transaction` - (Optional) You can use this parameter to transfer funds from a charge before they are added to your available balance. A pending balance will transfer immediately but the funds will not become available until the original charge becomes available. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-availability) for details. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `source_type` - (Optional) The source balance to use for this transfer. One of `bank_account`, `card`, or `fpx`. For most users, this will default to `card`. Possible values: `bank_account`, `card`, `fpx`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `transfer_group` - (Optional) A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the [Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers#transfer-options) for details. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `amount_reversed` - Amount in cents (or local equivalent) reversed (can be less than the amount attribute on the transfer if a partial reversal was issued).
* `balance_transaction` - Balance transaction that describes the impact of this transfer on your account balance.
* `created` - Time that this record of the transfer was first created.
* `destination_payment` - If the destination is a Stripe account, this will be the ID of the payment that the destination account received for the transfer.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `reversals` - A list of reversals that have been applied to the transfer. See [`reversals`](#reversals) below.
* `reversed` - Whether the transfer has been fully reversed. If the transfer is only partially reversed, this attribute will still be false.

<a id="reversals"></a>
### `reversals`

The `reversals` attribute supports:

* `data` - Details about each object. See [`reversals.data`](#reversals.data) below.
* `has_more` - True if this list has another page of items after this one that can be fetched.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Always has the value `list`. Possible values: `list`.
* `url` - The URL where this list can be accessed.

<a id="reversals.data"></a>
### `reversals.data`

The `reversals.data` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `balance_transaction` - Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `destination_payment_refund` - Linked payment refund for the transfer reversal.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `transfer_reversal`.
* `source_refund` - ID of the refund responsible for the transfer reversal.
* `transfer` - ID of the transfer that was reversed.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a transfer whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_transfer.payout_share

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_transfer.payout_share
```

The transfer stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a transfer using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_transfer.payout_share
  id = "tr_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_transfer.payout_share
  identity = {
    id = "tr_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the transfer.

Using `terraform import`, import a transfer using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_transfer.payout_share tr_123
```
